name: Steal Web Session Cookie

evidence.rationale: Wiping managed browsers and application data removes locally stored enterprise session cookies before they can be extracted from a lost or stolen device.

Updating browsers, password managers, and related applications reduces exploitation of known vulnerabilities used to extract session cookies. It does not prevent cookie theft by malware or an adversary that already has sufficient access to browser storage or memory.

Remediating vulnerabilities in browsers and related applications reduces exploit-based extraction of session cookies. This does not prevent cookie theft by malware or an adversary that already has sufficient access to browser storage or memory.

Updating browsers reduces the likelihood that known vulnerabilities can be exploited to extract cookies from browser storage or memory. It does not prevent malware with sufficient local access from directly reading cookies or browser data.
Malicious browser extensions may access browser cookies and session information. Restricting extensions removes one important cookie-theft path.
Web filtering and application-layer gateways can block malicious content or destinations used to deliver browser-based session-cookie theft activity.

This relationship applies when penetration testing identifies the described software configuration weakness and remediation of the finding changes by configuring secure cookie attributes, shorter lifetimes, session invalidation, and reduced persistence in affected applications or browsers.
